fields.title: Polka: bonuses credited twice
fields.summary: 1,340 double creditings and 90 uncredited in a month. A campaign triple the size is coming.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do before the campaign? Name the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a customer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a Polka PM. Over a month, 1,340 cases of double bonus crediting. Total amount is around 380 thousand rubles in bonuses, of which roughly 40% was spent. Concurrently, 90 complaints about the opposite: bonuses not credited at all.
fields.brief/objective: Close both causes of bonus discrepancy before a campaign that triples volume.
fields.brief/constraints: Campaign in two weeks. Excess bonuses cannot be taken back per policy.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do before the campaign and justify the sequence.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: "At least once" means the handler must be idempotent
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A queue with this guarantee will eventually deliver a message twice—this is not a bug, but its contract. That means protection lives in the handler: a key by event identifier, not a hope that a duplicate won't arrive. And alongside is always the dead-letter queue: what wasn't delivered won't return on its own, and manual triage stops working the exact moment volume scales.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: The `order.created` event goes to a queue, the handler credits bonuses with the command "add N points to user". Delivery guarantee is at least once. Handler is not idempotent.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: "Duplicates are redeliveries, standard queue behavior. Not credited are messages that went to the dead-letter queue, there are 90 of them for the month, triaged manually and irregularly. Making it idempotent by order ID takes two days. Automated dead-letter queue triage takes a week."
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: Bonuses are credited at checkout, before payment confirmation.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: 4% of orders are canceled after checkout. Bonus deduction on cancellation works, but with double crediting it only deducts one portion.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Two days. Redelivery does not credit a second time.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: duplicates stop. The 90 uncredited remain—they are in the dead-letter queue, and that's a different cause. We make it before the campaign with a margin.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Idempotency plus automated dead-letter queue triage
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Idempotency plus automated dead-letter queue triage. A week and a half. Closes both problems.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: we make it. Duplicates stop, uncredited ones retry automatically, only unrepeatable ones hit manual triage. Requires deciding what counts as unrepeatable.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Reschedule crediting to payment confirmation moment
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: A week. Also eliminates crediting for unpaid orders.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: solves the adjacent problem with cancellations. Does not eliminate duplicates—same queue, same non-idempotency. Changes product behavior: bonuses don't appear immediately, needs explaining.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: A week. At night we reconcile crediting with orders, mark excess, add missing.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: catches both problems post-facto. Excess bonuses cannot be taken back per policy, so reconciliation only logs the damage. Does not fix the root cause, and with tripled volume in the campaign, damage triples too.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not understand the "at least once" guarantee as a norm
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not know how to make an operation idempotent by reformulation
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not read the dead-letter queue as a source of a separate class of problems
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Limits and surge protection are not treated as a product decision
